The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14223512/assets/ef837c5bdd4198651302e77b70d592c7771071a1ee3543ce76a3685b0439fa82.png)

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=-1$ and $y=-2,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines. 

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(x+1)(y+2) \\ {y}^{′} & =(x+1)^{2}(y+2)\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=-1$ and $y=-2$ divide the plane into $4$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $4$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| $y>-2$ | $↘$

$(-)$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-2$ | $↗$

$(+)$ | $↘$

$(-)$ |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |

Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=(x+1)(y+2).
$$
